Treatment summary
Patient presented following a low-speed head-on motor vehicle collision with
complaints of neck pain, stiffness, and headache consistent with a whiplash-type
mechanism. The reported injury is plausible given the mechanics of this crash. Over
the course of 30 visits, care included passive modalities, range-of-motion exercises,
and a progressive home exercise program, following a usual and expected course of
treatment. Visit frequency tapered as symptoms improved and the patient regained
functioanl range of motion. Examination revealed cervical paraspinal tenderness and
reduced range of motion that support the reported injury, while neurological screening
and certain orthopedic tests were within normal limits. No piror injury to the
cervical spine or upper back is known to this provider. Billing review is ongoing for
two similar charges recoredd on the same date of service, which are being verified
before final processing. Prognosis is good with continued home exercise and as-needed
follow-up.
